messages:
Priya Malhotra: FYI we're planning a focused EU cutover test next Wed for a small tenant cohort. Objective: validate proxy-driven failover + strict residency controls. Call out issues now.

Jon Kim: Quick clarifying Q: are we exercising active/active sticky routing or a promote-to-write active/passive path? Different failure modes.

Priya Malhotra: Both, but primary is active/active with soft affinity (client hints). Also exercise promote path that kicks in if local primary is degraded. Must ensure writes never land outside EU unless tenant opted-in.

Lina Ortega: Residency constraint restated: writes = EU-only by default. Reads may be multi-region if consented. For failovers we either promote local standby or fail-write; no automatic remote writes.

Marco Li: Operational flow proposal for proxy: respect X-Region-Hint, then try: (1) local primary, (2) local standby promote, (3) fail-with-readonly. We'll test KV cache rehydrate for promoted node. Need to ensure tokens are audited.

Jon Kim: Promotion requires a lease/fencing handshake with writer replicas. Otherwise split-brain risk. Suggest a leasing token with monotonic epoch and short TTL plus explicit fence operation.

Lina Ortega: Agreed. Lease model: epoch bump in control plane + read-after-write confirm from promoter. If promoter can't obtain fence, proxy must reject writes and surface operator action.

Ella Nguyen: Ops note: real VPC peering promote is slow. For the test we'll use a feature-flag that allows EU-standby to accept writes (annotated). Must produce a trace for every write indicating promote_reason and promote_epoch.

Priya Malhotra: Test plan (short): flip FF, run 5m traffic replay across 40 tenants. Validate: a) no non-EU write artifacts unless opt-in, b) KV warmup P95 < 250ms, c) lease handoff < 1s, d) audit entries for all promoted writes.

Marco Li: Test client for hinting:
```bash
curl -H "X-Region-Hint: eu-central-1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" https://proxy.redwood.internal/v1/complete -d '{"prompt":"ping"}'
```
Proxy should return X-Effective-Region header and X-Promote-Epoch when applicable.

Jon Kim: If promote can't complete, proxy should return 409 with code ERR_RESIDENCY_PROMOTE_FAILED and human-readable message. Should we auto-fallback to global readonly after a timeout?

Lina Ortega: No auto-global-writes. Auto-readonly is okay; auto-write to non-EU is a legal violation. If promote times out, surface error + alert. Manual override path for emergency export must require two operator approvals and extra logging.

Priya Malhotra: Decision for this test: soft-affinity active/active, promote-first behavior, fail-writes after 30s of unsuccessful promote. No automated global-write. Telemetry: counters for promote_attempts/promote_success/promote_latency/blocked_writes/promote_fail_reasons.

deploy-bot: canary deploy of proxy-service EU succeeded (tag: eu-cutover-test-2026-03).

Ella Nguyen: I'll own dashboard widgets and runbook blurb. Marco please own KV priming harness and traffic replay. Jon + Lina to own lease fencing code + audit schema. Priya to coordinate tenant selection and CSA notifications.

Marco Li: On it. I'll push a lightweight harness and instructions to infra repo and share steps here.

Jon Kim: I'll draft lease epoch API: POST /leases/{tenant} {proposed_epoch, fence_token} -> 200 with confirmed_epoch or 409. Gate proxy write path on confirmed_epoch match.

Lina Ortega: Audit schema draft: tenant_id | write_id | effective_region | promote_epoch | promote_reason | auditor_id. Keep it flat CSV-friendly.

Priya Malhotra: Thanks. Let's do a sync Mon EOD to finalize checklist. If no objections I'll schedule. :white_check_mark:
